answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making every identity hold a live, memory-hard working set probed at random. Each persona hashes its key into a structure dense as basalt, resident in RAM; verification probes mirror back fragments of that state. A clone cannot serve two identities from one shared region, since each persona's probes index a distinct address space. Running n identities costs n resident working sets; memory clones cannot pool, as one root cannot feed a whole orchard. Each extra identity needs its own always-on memory bank, so marginal cost never hits zero.
